title: The Price Impact of Hedging Expiring Index Options
one_line: Delta hedges of expiring cash-settled S&P 500 options are unwound at expiration; using proprietary market-maker positions, the authors find these unwinds move index-futures returns and volatility in the 30 minutes before expiration.

findings.statement: Hedge unwinding concentrated in the last 30 minutes before expiration.
Also documents volatility effects of hedge rebalancing.

why.pattern: Cash settlement means hedges must be traded away at expiry, creating predictable flow.

reported_results.headline: Delta hedges of expiring cash-settled S&P 500 options are unwound at expiration; using proprietary market-maker positions, the authors find these unwinds move index-futures returns and volatility in the 30 minutes before expiration.

tradable_edge: Supports a last-30-minutes look on PM-expiration days (third_friday_spike_es / expiration_pin_es descriptive check: 15:30-16:00 range and drift on expiration vs non-expiration days). Direction needs dealer positions we do not have.
data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project). Needs options positioning / open-interest data we do not have; ES/NQ price data only allows proxies.
caveats: Only the abstract / a secondary summary was reachable (SSRN is blocked from chat sessions); numbers not verified against the full paper.
